about: Public-notice channels per operator or agency: pages, sites, feeds, lists and accounts through which the public is told of sewage discharges, by law, permit or voluntarily. Read by pipeline/ingest/notification_pages.py (schema and validator there; test tests/test_notice_channels.py).

fields.id: unique channel id: '<state lower>-' then lowercase letters, digits and hyphens; stable (record ids and snapshots follow the URL, not the id, but merges and reviews follow the id)
fields.state: two-letter postal code of the jurisdiction (DC included)
fields.operator_id: data/dischargers.json id of the operator, or null for an agency or group channel
fields.agency: the agency or group that runs the channel when it is not an operator in data/dischargers.json, else null
fields.name: public name of the operator or agency
fields.permit: the NPDES / state permit the channel serves (one of the operator's npdes_permits), or null
fields.urls: the URL(s) read, http(s); [] only for a channel that is not monitored (none found, email only)
fields.method: how the URLs are read (enums.method); null only when urls is []
fields.legal_basis: the law or permit clause that makes it a public channel, cited; null only for voluntary
fields.monitored: true when this module fetches it
fields.unmonitored_reason: when monitored is false: why (enums.unmonitored_reason); null when monitored
fields.publishes: what the research saw on it (enums.publishes): a current status, a rainfall likelihood, dated notices, documents, only a link elsewhere, sampling results, nothing
fields.note: research note, internal (not exported); required for none_found and other
fields.checked: date the row was last checked against the source, YYYY-MM-DD
fields.barrier: what keeps the channel's notices off the open web (enums.barrier), from unmonitored_reason, the kind and the note (barrier_for); null for a monitored row or one read through a feed (feed_ingested), and for a row the register does not settle (then barrier_review says why)

optional_fields.authority: who is credited on records from this channel (default: name)
optional_fields.noun: the noun of the health wording (default 'Notification page', 'Voluntary page' for voluntary rows)
optional_fields.link_text: for link_only / likelihood rows: what the page links to ('the shared rainfall site'); the wording is 'Links to <link_text> only'
optional_fields.status_pattern: regular expression that finds the current status on the page; when it stops matching the wording says so
optional_fields.entry: {start, end}: regular expressions that cut this row's entry out of a page several rows share (from the first line matching start to the next line matching end)
optional_fields.ignore_lines: regular expressions of volatile lines (readings, clocks) left out of the text hash
optional_fields.records: false: never make records from this channel (default true)
optional_fields.dated_lines_are_notices: true: any added dated line is a notice (an event table)
optional_fields.default_event_type: event type of a notice whose words name none (common.EVENT_TYPES)
optional_fields.every_hours: fetch at most this often (default: every refresh)
optional_fields.headers: 'browser' to send a browser user agent (hosts that refuse others)
optional_fields.feed_source_id: for feed_ingested: the source id of the feed that reads it
optional_fields.signup_url: where the public signs up for its alerts, when it has a list
optional_fields.seeds: {url: [{path, fetched_at, http_status}]}: earlier copies (research, surveys) taken as the first snapshots, oldest first; path relative to the project root
optional_fields.sources: research or registry ids the row rests on
optional_fields.barrier_review: internal: why an unmonitored row has no barrier yet (listed in docs/reviews/2026-11-03-barriers.md)

rules: channels sorted by (state, id); ids unique
operator_id or agency is given; operator_id exists in data/dischargers.json; a permit given with an operator_id is one of that operator's npdes_permits
monitored rows have urls and a method; unmonitored rows have an unmonitored_reason
basis_kind law or permit has a legal_basis
barrier is null for monitored and feed_ingested rows, follows login, bot_wall and image_only, and is set (or barrier_review given) for every other unmonitored row
regular expressions compile; seeds name the row's urls

channels.name: Aspetuck Health District
channels.note: Aspetuck Health District beach results. Voluntary local beach results. (research/ct/report.md §2.8)

channels.name: City of Bridgeport WPCA - East Side WPCF (Seaview Ave) and East Side combined sewers
channels.note: Bridgeport WPCA (East Side): own CSO notice practice. Voluntary: no Connecticut law requires an operator's own web notice (2026 HB 5522 would have; it died in the Senate). As West Side. (research/ct/report.md §2.7)

channels.name: City of Bridgeport WPCA - West Side WPCF (Bostwick Ave) and West Side combined sewers
channels.note: Bridgeport WPCA (West Side): own CSO notice practice. Voluntary: no Connecticut law requires an operator's own web notice (2026 HB 5522 would have; it died in the Senate). City WPCA page shows a 'Notification:' heading with phone numbers only; operator under contract. (research/ct/report.md §2.7)

channels.name: Connecticut River Conservancy
channels.note: Connecticut River Conservancy, Is It Clean? (E. coli results). Voluntary volunteer and CRC lab results, weekly in season; 63+ CT sites. (research/ct/report.md §2.11)

channels.name: Connecticut CSO permittees
channels.note: No web form: Signs at CSO outfalls ("Wet Weather Sewage Discharge Outfall"). Basis not established in the research (the permit text, RCSA 22a-430-3, was not read); DEEP's 2026-07-07 release tells the public to look for physical CSO signs. No online record. Covers: ct-bridgeport-wpca-east, ct-bridgeport-wpca-west, ct-gnhwpca, ct-norwich-npu, ct-mdc-hartford. (research/ct/report.md §2.7)

channels.name: Connecticut DEEP
channels.legal_basis: CGS 22a-424a(c)(4): real-time public notification system
channels.note: DEEP Everbridge text and email spill alerts (announced pilot). Announced for fall 2026, sign-up by town; no sign-up page on 2026-11-01. Watch the SRTK page. Covers every operator in the state. (research/ct/report.md §2.6)

channels.name: Connecticut DEEP
channels.note: DEEP HazConnect public incident list (live spill log). Voluntary publication of CGS 22a-450 reports; behind a Cloudflare bot check. https://connecticut.hazconnect.com/listincidentpublic.aspx answered 403 to the project user agent on 2026-11-03. (research/ct/report.md §2.5)

channels.name: Connecticut DEEP
channels.legal_basis: CGS 22a-424a(b) and (c)(1): DEEP posts each spill or bypass report on its website within 2 hours of receipt, with a current map
channels.note: DEEP Performance Dashboard (Bypass / CSO Live Map; QAlert reports in Zoho Analytics). 2026 CSO rows lack the outfall group and receiving water for every utility but Bridgeport East. Covers every operator in the state. (research/ct/report.md §2.1-2.2)

channels.name: Connecticut DEEP
channels.note: DEEP news releases (large spills, seasonal rain reminders). Voluntary: no statute requires a press release; DEEP issued one for the 2025 East Windsor break and the 2026-07-07 rain reminder. Sign-up status: confirmed (email) (docs/subscriptions.md). (research/ct/report.md §2.6, §2.12)

channels.name: Connecticut DEEP
channels.note: DEEP Emergency Response spill log, data.ct.gov ffju-s5c5. Voluntary publication: spills are reported to DEEP under CGS 22a-450; the monthly dataset is DEEP's practice. Covers every operator in the state. (research/ct/report.md §2.5)

channels.name: Connecticut DEEP
channels.legal_basis: CGS 22a-424a(c)(5): annual report by February 1
channels.note: DEEP Sewage Right to Know page and annual reports (xlsx, PDF). Covers every operator in the state. (research/ct/report.md §2.4)

channels.name: Connecticut DEEP
channels.note: State Swimming Water Quality Report (state park beaches). Voluntary state park beach status, in season only. (research/ct/report.md §2.8)

channels.name: Connecticut DEEP
channels.legal_basis: CGS 22a-424a(c)(4): real-time public notification system within 2 hours of DEEP's receipt (DEEP says the X account meets it)
channels.note: DEEP X account @CTSewageSpills ("CT Sewer Overflows"). Posted by hand; X cannot be read without its API. Covers every operator in the state. (research/ct/report.md §2.6)

channels.agency: Connecticut Department of Agriculture, Bureau of Aquaculture
channels.name: Connecticut Department of Agriculture, Bureau of Aquaculture
channels.note: DoAg recreational shellfish hotlines and closure maps. Closures after rainfall announced by town phone lines and PDF maps; no statute cited in the research. (research/ct/report.md §2.10)

channels.name: Connecticut Department of Public Health
channels.note: DPH Beach Advisory portal (beachadvisory.ct.gov) with alert sign-up. Voluntary: closures follow DPH/DEEP guidelines (2016), not a statute; a sewage bypass may close a beach before sampling. TLS certificate expired on 2026-11-01. https://beachadvisory.ct.gov/ answered tls to the project user agent on 2026-11-03. (research/ct/report.md §2.8)

channels.name: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (ECHO)
channels.note: EPA ECHO sewer overflow and bypass event records (NPDES eReporting). Voluntary publication by EPA: operators must report noncompliance to the permitting authority within 24 hours (40 CFR 122.41(l)(6)); EPA publishes the electronic reports. . Covers every operator in the state. (research/federal/report.md)

channels.name: Farmington River Watershed Association
channels.note: Farmington River Watershed Association bacteria results. Voluntary sampling; also shown on Is It Clean?. (research/ct/report.md §2.11)

channels.name: Greater New Haven Water Pollution Control Authority (East Shore WPAF)
channels.note: Greater New Haven WPCA: own CSO notice practice. Voluntary: no Connecticut law requires an operator's own web notice (2026 HB 5522 would have; it died in the Senate). gnhwpca.com: CSO documents and construction alerts only. (research/ct/report.md §2.7)

channels.name: Harbor Watch
channels.note: Harbor Watch (Earthplace) Fairfield County River Report. Voluntary; raw data in the Water Quality Portal, annual report. (research/ct/report.md §2.11)

channels.name: Interstate Environmental Commission
channels.note: Interstate Environmental Commission pathogen monitoring network. Voluntary; western Long Island Sound. https://www.iec-nynjct.org/node/384 answered connection to the project user agent on 2026-11-03. (research/ct/report.md §2.11)

channels.name: Ledge Light Health District
channels.note: Ledge Light Health District beach results. Voluntary local beach results; HTTP 522 on 2026-11-01. (research/ct/report.md §2.8)

channels.name: Connecticut local health departments (others)
channels.note: Other local health departments' beach closures (Fairfield, Greenwich, Milford, New Haven, Stamford). Voluntary; pages not found in search. (research/ct/report.md §2.8)

Voluntary page; fetched 2026-11-04. Snapshot only for now (records false): the lines are not yet parsed into records. (research/fl/report.md §2.3)

channels.name: Sarasota County
channels.note: Sarasota County's AbnormalEventSpill layer: sanitary sewer overflows in the county reported to DEP by the North Port, Sarasota and Venice utilities, the Englewood district, Sarasota County Utilities and private systems (date, type, gallons, whether surface water was affected, a point). Voluntary: a county publication no law requires. The layer's description answered 200 to the project user agent on 2026-11-04 (last edit 2026-08-17). Only the description is read (its last-edit time shows a change): the rows carry street addresses and free-text notes, and the PNP feed (fl-dep-pnp) carries the same reportable events. (research/fl/report.md, fl-sarasota-abnormal-event)

channels.name: A&D Water Service Inc
channels.legal_basis: G.S. 143-215.1C(a): "The owner or operator of any wastewater collection or treatment works, the operation of which is primarily to collect or treat municipal or domestic wastewater and for which a permit is issued under this Part and having an average annual flow greater than 200,000 gallons per day, shall provide to the users or customers of the collection system or treatment works and to the Department an annual report that summarizes the performance of the collection system or treatment works and the extent to which the collection system or treatment works has violated the permit or federal or State laws, regulations, or rules related to the protection of water quality. The report shall be prepared on either a calendar or fiscal year basis and shall be provided no later than 60 days after the end of the calendar or fiscal year."
channels.note: No web form: A&D Water Service Inc: the yearly report on the system's performance and its permit violations goes to the users or customers and a copy to the Department (DEQ), no later than 60 days after the calendar or fiscal year; the law requires no web posting. It summarizes the year, not single overflows. The duty applies to municipal or domestic works with an average annual flow over 200,000 gallons a day: flow not checked: no design flow is on record for WQCSD0368 (a collection system or a plant missing from EPA's rows); listed on the side of caution. The operator's own posting was not searched individually. (G.S. 143-215.1C(a), read on ncleg.gov 2026-11-04)

channels.name: A&D Water Service Inc
channels.legal_basis: G.S. 143-215.1C(b)(2): "In the event of a discharge of 15,000 gallons or more of untreated wastewater to the surface waters of the State, publish a notice of the discharge in a newspaper having general circulation in the county in which the discharge occurs and in each county downstream from the point of discharge that is significantly affected by the discharge." The notice is captioned "NOTICE OF DISCHARGE OF UNTREATED SEWAGE" and published within 10 days after the Secretary approves its form, content and newspapers
channels.note: No web form: A&D Water Service Inc (municipal or domestic works, public or private, so (b)): a paid notice in newspapers of the county and of each downstream county the Secretary finds significantly affected, for 15,000 gallons or more; proof of publication is filed with DEQ within 30 days. Printed only; the law requires no web posting. (G.S. 143-215.1C, read on ncleg.gov 2026-11-04; research/nc/report.md §2.1)

channels.name: A&D Water Service Inc
channels.legal_basis: G.S. 143-215.1C(b)(1): "In the event of a discharge of 1,000 gallons or more of untreated wastewater to the surface waters of the State, issue a press release to all print and electronic news media that provide general coverage in the county where the discharge occurred setting out the details of the discharge. The owner or operator shall issue the press release within 24 hours after the owner or operator has determined that the discharge has reached the surface waters of the State."
channels.note: No web form: A&D Water Service Inc (municipal or domestic works, public or private, so (b)): a press release to all print and electronic news media covering the county within 24 hours after it determines that 1,000 gallons or more reached surface waters. It reaches the public printed only or on air, as the media carry it; the law requires no web posting. Copies and the media list are kept a year and given to any person on request. (G.S. 143-215.1C, read on ncleg.gov 2026-11-04; research/nc/report.md §2.1)

channels.note: No web form: Town of Bath: the yearly report on the system's performance and its permit violations goes to the users or customers and a copy to the Department (DEQ), no later than 60 days after the calendar or fiscal year; the law requires no web posting. It summarizes the year, not single overflows. The duty applies to municipal or domestic works with an average annual flow over 200,000 gallons a day: flow not checked: no design flow is on record for WQCSD0068 (a collection system or a plant missing from EPA's rows); listed on the side of caution. The operator's own posting was not searched individually. (G.S. 143-215.1C(a), read on ncleg.gov 2026-11-04)

channels.name: Town of Bath

channels.note: No web form: Town of Creswell (municipal or domestic works, public or private, so (b)): a paid notice in newspapers of the county and of each downstream county the Secretary finds significantly affected, for 15,000 gallons or more; proof of publication is filed with DEQ within 30 days. Printed only; the law requires no web posting. (G.S. 143-215.1C, read on ncleg.gov 2026-11-04; research/nc/report.md §2.1)

channels.name: Town of Creswell
channels.legal_basis: G.S. 143-215.1C(b)(1): "In the event of a discharge of 1,000 gallons or more of untreated wastewater to the surface waters of the State, issue a press release to all print and electronic news media that provide general coverage in the county where the discharge occurred setting out the details of the discharge. The owner or operator shall issue the press release within 24 hours after the owner or operator has determined that the discharge has reached the surface waters of the State."
channels.note: No web form: Town of Creswell (municipal or domestic works, public or private, so (b)): a press release to all print and electronic news media covering the county within 24 hours after it determines that 1,000 gallons or more reached surface waters. It reaches the public printed only or on air, as the media carry it; the law requires no web posting. Copies and the media list are kept a year and given to any person on request. (G.S. 143-215.1C, read on ncleg.gov 2026-11-04; research/nc/report.md §2.1)

channels.name: Currituck County
channels.legal_basis: G.S. 143-215.1C(a): "The owner or operator of any wastewater collection or treatment works, the operation of which is primarily to collect or treat municipal or domestic wastewater and for which a permit is issued under this Part and having an average annual flow greater than 200,000 gallons per day, shall provide to the users or customers of the collection system or treatment works and to the Department an annual report that summarizes the performance of the collection system or treatment works and the extent to which the collection system or treatment works has violated the permit or federal or State laws, regulations, or rules related to the protection of water quality. The report shall be prepared on either a calendar or fiscal year basis and shall be provided no later than 60 days after the end of the calendar or fiscal year."
channels.note: No web form: Currituck County: the yearly report on the system's performance and its permit violations goes to the users or customers and a copy to the Department (DEQ), no later than 60 days after the calendar or fiscal year; the law requires no web posting. It summarizes the year, not single overflows. The duty applies to municipal or domestic works with an average annual flow over 200,000 gallons a day: flow not checked: no design flow is on record for WQCS00273 (a collection system or a plant missing from EPA's rows); listed on the side of caution. The operator's own posting was not searched individually. (G.S. 143-215.1C(a), read on ncleg.gov 2026-11-04)

The report shall be prepared on either a calendar or fiscal year basis and shall be provided no later than 60 days after the end of the calendar or fiscal year."
channels.note: No web form: City of Eden: the yearly report on the system's performance and its permit violations goes to the users or customers and a copy to the Department (DEQ), no later than 60 days after the calendar or fiscal year; the law requires no web posting. It summarizes the year, not single overflows. The duty applies to municipal or domestic works with an average annual flow over 200,000 gallons a day: EPA's permitted (design) flow for NC0025071 is 13.5 MGD, over the threshold; the average annual flow the law counts was not checked. The operator's own posting was not searched individually. (G.S. 143-215.1C(a), read on ncleg.gov 2026-11-04)

channels.name: City of Eden
channels.legal_basis: G.S. 143-215.1C(b)(2): "In the event of a discharge of 15,000 gallons or more of untreated wastewater to the surface waters of the State, publish a notice of the discharge in a newspaper having general circulation in the county in which the discharge occurs and in each county downstream from the point of discharge that is significantly affected by the discharge." The notice is captioned "NOTICE OF DISCHARGE OF UNTREATED SEWAGE" and published within 10 days after the Secretary approves its form, content and newspapers
channels.note: No web form: City of Eden (municipal or domestic works, public or private, so (b)): a paid notice in newspapers of the county and of each downstream county the Secretary finds significantly affected, for 15,000 gallons or more; proof of publication is filed with DEQ within 30 days. Printed only; the law requires no web posting. (G.S. 143-215.1C, read on ncleg.gov 2026-11-04; research/nc/report.md §2.1)

channels.name: City of Eden
channels.legal_basis: G.S. 143-215.1C(b)(1): "In the event of a discharge of 1,000 gallons or more of untreated wastewater to the surface waters of the State, issue a press release to all print and electronic news media that provide general coverage in the county where the discharge occurred setting out the details of the discharge. The owner or operator shall issue the press release within 24 hours after the owner or operator has determined that the discharge has reached the surface waters of the State."
channels.note: No web form: City of Eden (municipal or domestic works, public or private, so (b)): a press release to all print and electronic news media covering the county within 24 hours after it determines that 1,000 gallons or more reached surface waters. It reaches the public printed only or on air, as the media carry it; the law requires no web posting. Copies and the media list are kept a year and given to any person on request. (G.S. 143-215.1C, read on ncleg.gov 2026-11-04; research/nc/report.md §2.1)

channels.name: Town of Newton Grove
channels.legal_basis: G.S. 143-215.1C(b)(2): "In the event of a discharge of 15,000 gallons or more of untreated wastewater to the surface waters of the State, publish a notice of the discharge in a newspaper having general circulation in the county in which the discharge occurs and in each county downstream from the point of discharge that is significantly affected by the discharge." channels.name: Town of Newton Grove
channels.legal_basis: G.S. 143-215.1C(b)(1): "In the event of a discharge of 1,000 gallons or more of untreated wastewater to the surface waters of the State, issue a press release to all print and electronic news media that provide general coverage in the county where the discharge occurred setting out the details of the discharge. channels.note: No web form: Town of Newton Grove (municipal or domestic works, public or private, so (b)): a press release to all print and electronic news media covering the county within 24 hours after it determines that 1,000 gallons or more reached surface waters. (G.S. 143-215.1C, read on ncleg.gov 2026-11-04; research/nc/report.md §2.1)

The notice is captioned "NOTICE OF DISCHARGE OF UNTREATED SEWAGE" and published within 10 days after the Secretary approves its form, content and newspapers
channels.note: No web form: Town of Ramseur (municipal or domestic works, public or private, so (b)): a paid notice in newspapers of the county and of each downstream county the Secretary finds significantly affected, for 15,000 gallons or more; proof of publication is filed with DEQ within 30 days. Printed only; the law requires no web posting. (G.S. 143-215.1C, read on ncleg.gov 2026-11-04; research/nc/report.md §2.1)

channels.name: Town of Ramseur
channels.legal_basis: G.S. 143-215.1C(b)(1): "In the event of a discharge of 1,000 gallons or more of untreated wastewater to the surface waters of the State, issue a press release to all print and electronic news media that provide general coverage in the county where the discharge occurred setting out the details of the discharge. The owner or operator shall issue the press release within 24 hours after the owner or operator has determined that the discharge has reached the surface waters of the State."
channels.note: No web form: Town of Ramseur (municipal or domestic works, public or private, so (b)): a press release to all print and electronic news media covering the county within 24 hours after it determines that 1,000 gallons or more reached surface waters. It reaches the public printed only or on air, as the media carry it; the law requires no web posting. Copies and the media list are kept a year and given to any person on request. (G.S. 143-215.1C, read on ncleg.gov 2026-11-04; research/nc/report.md §2.1)

channels.name: City of Randleman
channels.legal_basis: G.S. 143-215.1C(a): "The owner or operator of any wastewater collection or treatment works, the operation of which is primarily to collect or treat municipal or domestic wastewater and for which a permit is issued under this Part and having an average annual flow greater than 200,000 gallons per day, shall provide to the users or customers of the collection system or treatment works and to the Department an annual report that summarizes the performance of the collection system or treatment works and the extent to which the collection system or treatment works has violated the permit or federal or State laws, regulations, or rules related to the protection of water quality. The report shall be prepared on either a calendar or fiscal year basis and shall be provided no later than 60 days after the end of the calendar or fiscal year."

The report shall be prepared on either a calendar or fiscal year basis and shall be provided no later than 60 days after the end of the calendar or fiscal year."
channels.note: No web form: City of Southport: the yearly report on the system's performance and its permit violations goes to the users or customers and a copy to the Department (DEQ), no later than 60 days after the calendar or fiscal year; the law requires no web posting. It summarizes the year, not single overflows. The duty applies to municipal or domestic works with an average annual flow over 200,000 gallons a day: flow not checked: no design flow is on record for WQCS00137 (a collection system or a plant missing from EPA's rows); listed on the side of caution. The operator's own posting was not searched individually. (G.S. 143-215.1C(a), read on ncleg.gov 2026-11-04)

channels.name: City of Southport
channels.legal_basis: G.S. 143-215.1C(b)(2): "In the event of a discharge of 15,000 gallons or more of untreated wastewater to the surface waters of the State, publish a notice of the discharge in a newspaper having general circulation in the county in which the discharge occurs and in each county downstream from the point of discharge that is significantly affected by the discharge." The notice is captioned "NOTICE OF DISCHARGE OF UNTREATED SEWAGE" and published within 10 days after the Secretary approves its form, content and newspapers
channels.note: No web form: City of Southport (municipal or domestic works, public or private, so (b)): a paid notice in newspapers of the county and of each downstream county the Secretary finds significantly affected, for 15,000 gallons or more; proof of publication is filed with DEQ within 30 days. Printed only; the law requires no web posting. (G.S. 143-215.1C, read on ncleg.gov 2026-11-04; research/nc/report.md §2.1)

channels.name: City of Southport
channels.legal_basis: G.S. 143-215.1C(b)(1): "In the event of a discharge of 1,000 gallons or more of untreated wastewater to the surface waters of the State, issue a press release to all print and electronic news media that provide general coverage in the county where the discharge occurred setting out the details of the discharge. The owner or operator shall issue the press release within 24 hours after the owner or operator has determined that the discharge has reached the surface waters of the State."
channels.note: No web form: City of Southport (municipal or domestic works, public or private, so (b)): a press release to all print and electronic news media covering the county within 24 hours after it determines that 1,000 gallons or more reached surface waters. It reaches the public printed only or on air, as the media carry it; the law requires no web posting. Copies and the media list are kept a year and given to any person on request. (G.S. 143-215.1C, read on ncleg.gov 2026-11-04; research/nc/report.md §2.1)
